text: If a straight-line falling across two straight-lines makes  the alternate angles equal to one another then the (two) straight-lines will be parallel to one another.  For let the straight-line $EF$, falling across the two straight-lines $AB$ and $CD$, make the alternate angles $AEF$ and $EFD$ equal to one another. I say that $AB$ and $CD$ are parallel.
For if not, being produced, $AB$ and $CD$ will certainly meet together: either in the direction of $B$ and $D$, or (in the direction) of $A$ and $C$ [Def.~1.23].
assertion: if AB and CD are not parallel, being produced they meet either toward B,D or toward A,C

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: $AB$ and $CD$ will certainly meet together: either in the direction of $B$ and $D$, or (in the direction) of $A$ and $C$

text: Let them have been produced, and let them meet together in the direction of $B$ and $D$ at  (point) $G$.
So, for the triangle $GEF$, the external angle $AEF$ is equal to the interior and opposite (angle) $EFG$.
assertion: for triangle GEF, external angle AEF equals interior opposite angle EFG

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: external angle $AEF$ is equal to the interior and opposite (angle) $EFG$

assertion: this is impossible (contradicts the exterior angle inequality)

text: Thus, being produced, $AB$ and $CD$ will not meet together in the direction of $B$ and $D$.
assertion: AB and CD do not meet in the direction of B and D

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: $AB$ and $CD$ will not meet together in the direction of $B$ and $D$

text: Similarly,  it can be shown that neither (will they meet together) in (the direction of) $A$ and $C$.
assertion: AB and CD do not meet in the direction of A and C either

spans.text: neither (will they meet together) in (the direction of) $A$ and $C$

text: But  (straight-lines) meeting in neither direction are parallel [Def.~1.23].
assertion: straight-lines meeting in neither direction are parallel

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: (straight-lines) meeting in neither direction are parallel

text: Thus, if a straight-line falling across two straight-lines makes  the alternate angles equal to one another then the (two) straight-lines will be parallel (to one another). (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
